clue.text: Web woven into bard's description of a horse

indicators.note: into tells us the reworked letters go inside the word for a bard

parts.note: a skald is a Norse poet or bard; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: woven suggests the strands of the word Web are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A poet's verse describes a horse, with a web woven into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container; a skald is an old Norse court poet. 'description of a horse' fits because the answer is an adjective for a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewbald is an adjective for a horse with patches of white and another colour, so it describes the animal's coat.

clue.text: This should remind you to hold your liquor

parts.note: to hold something is to keep it
sake is Japanese rice wine, a liquor

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who drinks: keep your drink down, or this will remind you.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept to bring back memories of a person or place.

clue.text: Labour committee

parts.note: looks like a group from the British Labour Party, but reads as a group of people formed to do a job of work and report back

explanation.definitionFit: A small group appointed to study a question and report, so a committee that labours.

clue.text: A wise old man, about 100 — he's relatively older

indicators.note: about means the name of the sage goes around the Roman numeral

parts.note: Nestor was the wise old counsellor of the Greeks in Homer
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A sage of about a hundred is described as being older than his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C (100) inside NESTOR, Homer's wise old Greek king, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear in one's family line is older by relationship, a pun on 'relatively' meaning as a relative.

clue.text: Cry of pain young girl is first to issue

indicators.note: is first says the word for the young girl comes before the cry of pain

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering society
ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: A young girl cries out in pain before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To debouch is to emerge or come out, as troops or a river from a narrow place into open ground.

clue.text: Run its course

definitions.meaning: to rush along at high speed
the progress of one's working life

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means rush headlong; as a noun it is the course of someone's professional life.

clue.text: Venture mountain climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the mountain's name reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A risky trip climbing a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ETNA upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake put into the pot before a poker deal, risked or ventured as a wager.

clue.text: Friend subjected to hostility, following the medieval custom

indicators.note: subjected to puts the friend's word beneath the hostility in this down clue

parts.note: a feud is long-running hostility
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend faces hostility, in the manner of the Middle Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'subjected to' places ALLY under FEUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The feudal system of lords and vassals was the medieval order, so this adverb means in that manner.

clue.text: One who's tested an explosive device in running water

indicators.note: in shows the device goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
an gives the article A
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone checks a bomb found in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' looks like any stream but means a particular river: the Exe in Devon, south-west England. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting an exam is the person being tested.

clue.text: He succeeded in the Irish Derby

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words the Irish

explanation.surface: He won the Irish Derby horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tHE IRish'; 'succeeded' means came after, not won.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inherits takes over from a predecessor, coming after them.

clue.text: During the Reign of Terror, it was difficult to stay calm

definitions.text: During the Reign of Terror, it was difficult to stay calm

parts.words: During the Reign of Terror, it was difficult to stay calm
parts.note: in revolutionary France the guillotine made it literally hard not to lose a body part, while the phrase also means staying composed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remain composed in a crisis, and literally to avoid beheading.

clue.text: I forgot he had concocted homoeopathic remedy

indicators.note: concocted means mixed up, so the words I forgot he had are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone forgot they had made up a homoeopathic remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken to cure a hangover works on the like-cures-like principle of homoeopathy.

clue.text: Painting finally framed by artist — it's very attractive

indicators.note: framed by puts the letter inside the painter's name, like a picture in a frame

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of Painting

explanation.surface: A painting finished and framed by an artist proves very popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives G, the end of Painting; 'framed by' sets it inside MANET.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron or lodestone that draws metal to it is attractive in the physical sense.

clue.text: Important cleric

definitions.meaning: a senior churchman of the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.definitionFit: The word means principal or fundamental, and also names a prince of the Catholic Church who elects the pope.

clue.text: One working for a short time, a long time, or a medium

parts.words: One working for a short time
parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A list of jobs: a temporary worker, someone for the long term, or a psychic medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting medium of pigment bound with egg yolk, used before oils.

clue.text: Send up underwear in a carrier

indicators.note: in means the undergarment goes inside the carrier

parts.note: a tray is something to carry things on
a vest is a British undergarment worn under a shirt

explanation.surface: Underwear is sent off in a carrier bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' is the definition, a verb meaning to mock. In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mock by grotesque imitation, which is what a parody or send-up does.

clue.text: I abandoned instrument to work on rig

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter I is dropped from the instrument

parts.note: a piano is a musical instrument
to ply is to work steadily at, as in ply a trade

explanation.surface: Someone gave up a musical instrument to work on an oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I abandoned' removes I from PIANO to leave PANO; 'rig' is the definition, not an oil platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A full suit of armour or complete outfit, which is what rig means as clothing or equipment.

clue.text: A house, we hear

parts.note: a theatre house is its crowd, and the crowd are the ones who listen; also a formal hearing

explanation.definitionFit: The spectators in a theatre are its house, and a formal interview or hearing is also an audience.

clue.text: Melanin's synthesised, that's official

indicators.note: synthesised means the letters of the pigment's name are made into something new

parts.note: taken with its S as fodder

explanation.surface: Skin pigment is made in the body, and that is official.
explanation.definitionFit: A match official who rules on balls crossing the line, an assistant referee.

clue.text: Saw in place, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us a word for in place is heard, not spelt

parts.note: sited means located or placed

explanation.surface: A tool on site, apparently noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: SITED and the answer are pronounced alike; 'Saw' is the verb, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Having caught sight of something means to have seen or spotted it.

clue.text: Little boys, replaced in team, riot

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are set in new places

explanation.surface: Youngsters swapped into a team cause a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupids, the chubby winged infants of Renaissance art, are little loves depicted as small children.

clue.text: Twopenny-halfpenny tankard?

definitions.meaning: British for cheap, petty or insignificant
a drinking mug made of tin, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means petty or worthless; read literally, a pot of tin is a metal drinking vessel.

clue.text: Fond of performing without a shirt

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the shirt goes in the middle

parts.note: doing means carrying out or performing
a T is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Keen on acting bare-chested.
explanation.walkthrough: The '3' in the held clue is a stray mark on the page. 'without' means outside here: DOING goes around T, as in T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fond of someone to excess, showing extravagant affection.

clue.text: Inviting one, they say, to be represented in point-to-point.

annotationWithheld.why: Inviting one, they say, to be represented in point-to-point. (4,2,3,3): 'Inviting' defines it, but no parse of the rest builds the letters without words doing double duty
annotationWithheld.clue: Inviting one, they say, to be represented in point-to-point.

clue.text: Active agent enlisting a sleeper at last

indicators.note: enlisting means the agent takes the letter into his ranks

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: at last takes the end letter of sleeper

explanation.surface: A secret agent recruits a sleeper, finally getting busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives R from sleeper; 'enlisting' puts it inside SPY. A sleeper is also a dormant spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and lively, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Curse mother uttered

indicators.note: uttered tells us the word for mother is spoken, not written

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother swore out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM, an animal's mother, is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath or swearword used as an expletive.

clue.text: Boring passion's featured in book

indicators.note: featured in means the passion appears inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger or passion, with 's giving IRES

explanation.surface: Dull love story in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' is the container signal; the 's of passion's adds an S to the word for anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious and wearying, as something dull is.

clue.text: Cleaning out the bottom of extremely drear border

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters of drear

parts.note: edging is a border or trim

explanation.surface: Tidying up the base of a very dreary fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes D and R, the first and last letters of drear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooping silt and mud from a riverbed or harbour floor.
